root_cause.text: In the i915 display driver, `unlink_nv12_plane()` was called after `plane_atomic_check()` had already computed the new plane state, causing it to overwrite the correctly computed state when a plane previously used as an NV12 Y‑plane was reconfigured as a normal plane; this was made worse by the prior removal of a visibility check that had previously prevented the state clobbering.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states, "unlink_nv12_plane() will clobber parts of the plane state potentially already set up by plane_atomic_check(), so we must make sure not to call the two in the wrong order." It also notes, "This used to work on account of unlink_nv12_plane() skipping the state clearing based on the plane visibility. But I removed that check." The patch moves the `unlink_nv12_plane()` call earlier (e.g., into `intel_plane_set_invisible()` and before `icl_check_nv12_planes()` processes new state) and adds a guard for `planar_linked_plane` being NULL.
